claims.text: Single-phase fcc FeCoNi and its single-phase fcc high-entropy-alloy derivatives have reported coercive fields no greater than 100 Oe.
Introducing a controlled second magnetic phase into an fcc FeCoNi matrix will increase its coercive field above 100 Oe.
Compositional tuning or heat treatment can form a bcc or ordered-intermetallic secondary phase in an fcc FeCoNi matrix.
Adding Al or Ti at greater than 5 at.% and applying heat treatment can induce a two-phase FeCoNi-based microstructure.
Annealing at 600–900 °C for several hours promotes phase separation or ordering in the proposed FeCoNiAl or FeCoNiTi alloys.
The intervention will produce a dispersed bcc or ordered-intermetallic magnetic phase within the fcc matrix.
The resulting secondary phase will create phase boundaries and precipitates.
The secondary phase and its interfaces will act as domain-wall-pinning sites.
The secondary phase will introduce additional magnetic anisotropy.
Domain-wall pinning and additional magnetic anisotropy will hinder domain-wall motion and thereby increase coercivity.
The coercive field may reach several hundred Oe.
Coercivity enhancement requires the secondary phase to be magnetic and well dispersed.
The proposed effect does not apply to single-phase fcc, nanocrystalline, or amorphous states.
The magnitude of the coercivity increase depends on the volume fraction, distribution, and nature of the secondary phase.
Failure to exceed 100 Oe in a sample confirmed to contain a two-phase microstructure with a magnetic secondary phase would falsify the hypothesis.
